findings.title: Hardcoded "min" suffix bypasses messages/en.json
findings.detail: The minutes label is rendered as a hardcoded `{item.blockMinutes} min` string in JSX. This violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing copy through messages/en.json) and is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase, which renders minutes via i18n everywhere else: `t("provider.minutesShort", { minutes })` (SessionsTable, IncomingRequests, provider dashboard), `t("summary.minutesValue", { minutes })` (session summary), and `t("receipt.minutes", { minutes })` (the receipt route in this same diff). The literal " min" will not localize.
findings.suggestion: Reuse an existing minutes message key (e.g. the diff already added `receipt.minutes` = "{minutes} min"), or add an `account.minutesShort` key, and render `t("...", { minutes: item.blockMinutes })` instead of the bare ` min` literal.

findings.title: Three dead message keys added but never referenced
findings.detail: This diff adds `account.removeFavorite` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?"), and `account.settingsHeading` ("Payment & settings") to the catalog, but grep across app/ and components/ shows zero usages of any of them. `account.removeFavorite` is also a duplicate of `favorite.remove` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), which is the key actually used by FavoriteButton. `account.settingsHeading` duplicates the used `account.settingsTitle`. `account.cancelConfirm` was evidently authored for a cancel confirmation that was never wired up (see related finding).
findings.suggestion: Remove the three unused keys. FavoriteButton already uses `favorite.remove`, and the settings pages use `account.settingsTitle`/`settingsLink`, so nothing else needs to change.

findings.title: Inconsistent boundary validation of ids vs sibling actions
findings.detail: Sibling actions in this same file validate their id inputs with Zod before touching the DB — `addFavorite` runs `uuid.safeParse(providerId)` and `rescheduleBooking` uses `rescheduleSchema` (bookingId: uuid). But `cancelBooking` passes `bookingId` straight into `.eq("id", bookingId)` with no uuid check, and `removeFavorite` passes `providerId` straight into `.eq("provider_id", providerId)` with no uuid check. Both still check role + ownership (cancelBooking compares customer_id; removeFavorite scopes by customer_id), so this is defense-in-depth/consistency rather than a hole, but it's the kind of boundary-validation gap CLAUDE.md rule 5 calls out and reads as an inconsistency next to the validated siblings.
findings.suggestion: Add `if (!uuid.safeParse(bookingId).success) return { ok: false, error: "Booking not found." };` at the top of cancelBooking, and the same `uuid.safeParse(providerId)` guard already used in addFavorite to removeFavorite, so all four actions validate ids uniformly.

findings.location: cancel(), lines 32-44 and the Cancel button at lines 1097-1104
findings.title: Cancel fires immediately with no confirmation, leaving cancelConfirm orphaned
findings.detail: The Cancel button calls `cancel(item.id)` directly on click, which immediately invokes the `cancelBooking` server action (a destructive action that can capture/charge the full block per the cancellation policy). There is no confirmation step, even though the diff added `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") to the catalog — that key is never used (see dead-keys finding), strongly implying a confirm dialog was intended but dropped. Reschedule got an inline confirm UI; cancel did not.
findings.suggestion: Either wire `account.cancelConfirm` into a confirmation (the codebase already has components/ui/Dialog for this), or, if instant-cancel is intentional, delete the orphaned cancelConfirm key. Pick one so the catalog and behavior agree.

findings.title: Provider-by-ids lookup duplicates the second query of listFavoriteProviders
findings.detail: The new `getApprovedProvidersByIds` repeats the exact provider-fetch block already inside `listFavoriteProviders`: `.from("providers").select(PUBLIC_PROVIDER_COLUMNS).in("id", ids).eq("status", "approved")`. The only difference is the return shape (Map vs array). Minor, but it's the same RLS-scoped read written twice.
findings.suggestion: Optional: have listFavoriteProviders call getApprovedProvidersByIds (or a shared private helper) and return its values, so the public-columns provider fetch lives in one place.

content.text:
I've completed the M12 customer-dashboard diff review for reuse/simplification issues. Here is a summary of what I found:

**Findings (all reported via StructuredOutput):**

1. **Medium — Hardcoded "min" suffix** in `components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx:77` (`{item.blockMinutes} min`). Bypasses `messages/en.json` (CLAUDE.md rule 7) and is inconsistent with every other minutes render in the codebase, all of which go through i18n keys like `provider.minutesShort` / `summary.minutesValue` / `receipt.minutes` (the last added in this same diff).

2. **Low — Three dead message keys** added in `messages/en.json`: `account.removeFavorite` (duplicate of the used `favorite.remove`), `account.cancelConfirm`, and `account.settingsHeading` (duplicate of used `account.settingsTitle`). None are referenced anywhere.

3. **Low — Inconsistent id validation** in `app/(customer)/account/actions.ts`: `cancelBooking` and `removeFavorite` skip the Zod/uuid boundary check that their siblings `addFavorite` and `rescheduleBooking` perform. Ownership is still enforced, so it's consistency/defense-in-depth.

4. **Low — Cancel has no confirmation** in `UpcomingBookings.tsx`: the Cancel button invokes the destructive `cancelBooking` action immediately on click, while the orphaned `account.cancelConfirm` key suggests a confirm dialog was intended and dropped.

5. **Low — Duplicated provider fetch**: the new `getApprovedProvidersByIds` repeats the exact RLS-scoped provider query already embedded in `listFavoriteProviders`.

No correctness bugs or security holes were introduced — RLS/ownership checks, the payments adapter boundary, integer-cents handling, and `lib/pricing.ts` usage are all respected in this diff. The findings are reuse/consistency/dead-code cleanups.
